identification: 8 pieces of (catalogued) sterling: a squat oval Regency/George III-form cream jug on a pedestal foot with reeded girdle band and gadroon/beaded rim (form of c.1800-1820 London jugs; looks period, about 12-14 cm long judged against the napkin rings, not obviously miniature despite the catalogue wording); an embossed egg cup with heart and lobed panels and rope rim; 4 napkin rings (one with bright-cut stars, one waisted octagonal, one reeded band with cartouche, one plain banded); a pair of Georgian-style bright-cut sugar tongs with feather edge; a beaded-handle salt spoon. Estimate A$120-200, current bid A$80.

viewing_check: Weigh the lot (each piece if possible) and set the max off the per-gram scale. Turn the jug over/look under the rim and handle for George III marks (lion passant, leopard head, date letter, king's head) and maker; measure it. Read marks on tongs (bowl backs), egg cup, napkin rings and salt spoon; look for EPNS or 'plate'. Note dents and splits.
